column1: # Street types. Columns: set, full form (upper case, words separated by single spaces), abbreviation as the authority prints it, variants (semicolon separated, same spelling rules).
# A type is written in full unless the line is longer than the authority's limit (La Poste 38 characters, bpost 50), then the abbreviation is used.

# afnor: La Poste, SP 8855 volume 2, section 3.3 "liste alphabétique des abréviations autorisées pour les types de voies", and the UPU France sheet (extract). Types without an abbreviation there have none here.

# bpost-fr, bpost-nl, bpost-de: bpost MassPost guide January 2025, section 1, 4.2 "Summary table of abbreviations for street types". Dutch and German types are the endings of a name (Dendermondestraat, Hauptstrasse).
# Types the authority lists no abbreviation for: recognized so the street name starts after them.

# Group B. Road types that start (or, in Maltese and Irish usage, hold) a street line, so a line that names a street but has no number is still a street line (UPU Italy: "CALLE DEL CRISTO CANNAREGIO 1678", "Piazza San Calisto" on the UPU Vatican sheet; UPU Spain: "Calle Huertas 18"; UPU Portugal: "R LEAL DA CAMARA 31"; UPU Malta: "Triq San Guzepp"; UPU Andorra: "CARRER AIGUETA 19"). The authorities publish no abbreviation table in these sheets, so the abbreviation column is empty and no type is rewritten; the variants are the usual abbreviations, recognized and left as written.
